rendered:
Energy density: the review dates LIB commercial debut to Since their commercial debut in 1991[1], and says the energy density increased from 150 to 250 Wh kg[2]. That is a rise by a factor of 1.67[3] (gravimetric), with no end year given for that range.

Battery cost: the review says the cost decreased from over $1000[4] in 2008[5] to around $130 kWh[6] in 2020[7]. That is a fall by a factor of at least 7.7[8]-fold, because the starting cost is only given as over $1000.

For comparison, the review notes that the U.S. Department of Energy aimed over the last decades to reduce LIB cost by nearly eightfold[9]. The stacked-block figure of the same trends is Fig. 11[10]
